steps.title: Open Trendora's home page
steps.narration: Let's take a tour of Trendora, starting on the home page where the current market regime is summarized at a glance.
steps.point_out: The regime chart appears right away, with no error banner or blank space.

steps.title: Check the Data Manager's honest status
steps.narration: Now let's visit the Data Manager, where new market data arrives. The status badge in the top bar is visible on every page and always reflects the backend's real, current health — never a guess, and never stuck mid-boot without saying so.
steps.point_out: The badge reads "Ready" with a green dot.

steps.title: See every backfill job that's ever run
steps.narration: Scrolling down, the Run history table keeps a permanent record of every data job that's completed — including ones that found nothing new to do.
steps.point_out: A zero-work run is explained plainly, not just silently marked "done" like a real one.

steps.title: Confirm the backfilled dates in Scanner Runs
steps.narration: Every date a backfill touched shows up here, each one an exact, immutable snapshot of what the scanner saw that day.
steps.point_out: Real dates in the "As of" column, each opening its own stored leaderboard.

steps.title: Try a wide date range
steps.narration: Back on the Data Manager, the backfill form accepts any historical range you like, with no artificial limit on how much history you can request in one go.

steps.title: No range cap enforced
steps.narration: Filling in an eleven-year span, from 2015 to today, is accepted without any warning or truncation — there's no cap on how much data a single request can cover.
steps.point_out: Notice there's no error message or size warning — just a normal, ready-to-submit form.

steps.title: Aggregates computed once, at ingest
steps.narration: One more look at the Job progress panel: everything it lists — including the forward-looking aggregates used elsewhere in the app — was computed once when the data arrived, not recalculated every time someone looks.
steps.point_out: The summary line lists "forward aggregates" among the things refreshed by that run.

steps.title: Every page is checked against a committed budget
steps.narration: Trendora doesn't just feel fast — every page's loading time is measured and checked against a budget committed in the project's own performance-budgets report, the same report that backs the backend's five-second boot promise.
steps.point_out: This stock detail page — scores, risk detail, and all — loads well inside its own committed budget.

steps.title: Heavy number-crunching never slows down the rest of the app
steps.narration: When Trendora computes a big batch of forward-looking evidence in the background, the rest of the app keeps answering normally the whole time — measured, not just claimed.
steps.point_out: Across a measured 68.79 s background computation window, Backtest's slowest reply was 7.1191 s and the health check's slowest was 0.2530 s — both inside budget — while memory peaked with 58.2 % headroom still free.

steps.title: Backtest evidence, served instantly from storage
steps.narration: At the latest date, Backtest doesn't calculate anything on the spot — it simply displays evidence that was already computed and stored ahead of time.
steps.point_out: The full forward-tested evidence panel renders immediately, with no refreshing banner and no waiting.

steps.title: An older date, served honestly while a new one warms up
steps.narration: Ask Backtest for a date whose own evidence hasn't finished computing yet, and it never leaves you staring at a blank spinner — it instantly shows the last complete version it has, clearly labeled, while the new one finishes in the background.
steps.point_out: A visible "Refreshing — showing the last complete evidence" banner disclosed exactly which older date was being shown and when it was generated, while the page still rendered full evidence in well under a second — never a blank wait.

steps.title: The banner disappears the moment the new evidence is ready
steps.narration: Once the background computation finishes, reloading the same date now shows its own freshly stored evidence — banner gone, nothing recomputed on the spot, just a normal read from storage.
steps.point_out: The refreshing banner is gone and this date's own forward-tested evidence now renders directly, exactly like the always-ready latest view.
